pageCache.pageTitle: Thatcham Park CE Primary - Nursery Provision
pageCache.text:
Nursery Provision
Why choose our Nursery?
At Thatcham Park, our nursery offers a strong and nurturing start for every child. Rooted in our vision, “Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11), we create a caring environment where children feel safe, valued and ready to learn.
We focus on building confidence, independence and strong early skills through play, talk and exploration. From the very beginning, children are supported to develop communication, friendships and a love of learning.
Our nursery is part of a wider school community, which means children benefit from a smooth transition into Reception and beyond. Strong relationships with families are at the heart of what we do, ensuring every child is supported to thrive.
At Thatcham Park, nursery is more than childcare—it is the start of a journey where every child is encouraged to flourish.
Starting early, growing together
We have worked hard to develop and expand our nursery provision with our new building so that we can support children early, helping them to feel safe, confident and ready to learn. This early start makes a real difference, enabling children to build strong foundations for the future.
A nurturing beginning
Our nursery provides a warm, welcoming and nurturing environment where children are known, valued and encouraged as individuals. Strong relationships sit at the heart of everything we do, helping children to develop confidence, independence and a sense of belonging.
Through play, talk and carefully planned experiences, children begin to develop the key skills they need, particularly in communication, social development and early learning. Our approach ensures that learning is meaningful, engaging and appropriate to each child’s stage of development.
Supporting children and families
We understand that starting school is an important step for both children and their families. Our nursery team works closely with parents and carers, building trusting relationships and offering support and guidance along the way.
By beginning this partnership early, we are able to respond to children’s needs quickly and effectively, ensuring that every child is supported to thrive.
Building strong foundations for the future
Our early provision has a clear impact on children’s readiness for school. Children leave our nursery confident, curious and ready to take the next steps in their learning journey.
At Thatcham Park, nursery is more than a starting point—it is the beginning of a journey where every child is encouraged, supported and able to flourish.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thatcham Park CE Primary - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
It is a real privilege to introduce myself as the Headteacher of Thatcham Park Church of England Primary and Nursery School and to welcome you to our school website.
Choosing a school for your child is an important decision. We know families want their children to be happy, safe and well supported. They also want them to enjoy learning, make good friends and be known by the adults around them. That is what we want for every child at Thatcham Park.
Our Christian vision, “Encourage one another and build each other up”, sits at the heart of school life. It guides our relationships and the way we support every child to grow in confidence. As a Church of England school, our Christian foundation shapes who we are and how we treat one another. We warmly welcome families of all backgrounds, faiths and beliefs. At Thatcham Park, our values of Community, Compassion, Respect, Wisdom, Thankfulness and Endurance are part of everyday life. They help children understand how to care for others, make good choices and demonstrate resilience.
We have high expectations for learning and want every child to flourish and make strong progress, whatever their starting point. Children should leave Thatcham Park with secure foundations and a real sense of what they are capable of.
Just as importantly, we want children to enjoy their time with us. Primary school should be full of friendship, discovery and memorable experiences. It should give children the confidence to try new things and the freedom to develop their own interests.
Parents and carers are an important part of our school community. We believe children do best when home and school work closely together, so we place great value on positive relationships with families.
Thank you for visiting our website. I hope it gives you a sense of life at Thatcham Park and what we want for every child. If you are considering our school, we would be very pleased to welcome you for a tour and give you the opportunity to see our vision in action.
A caring, inclusive community
Strong support for every child, including SEND

pageCache.text:
Mental Health and Well-being
“There is a clear moral ethos of nurturing every pupil to help them achieve.” — Ofsted Inspection Report
At Thatcham Park, we place great importance on mental health and wellbeing. We recognise that wellbeing is fundamental to enabling every child to flourish. This is central to our vision:
“Encourage one another and build each other up”
(1 Thessalonians 5:11).
We believe that children learn best when they feel safe, valued and supported. Our approach to wellbeing ensures that every child is encouraged to develop confidence, resilience and a strong sense of belonging.
A caring and supportive environment
We work hard to create a calm, positive and nurturing environment where children feel safe and respected. Children are encouraged to talk about their thoughts and feelings and to know that they will be listened to.
We recognise that mental and physical health are equally important. By prioritising wellbeing, we aim to help every child feel secure, understood and ready to learn.
Supporting children to thrive
We understand that children may face different challenges at different times. Our role is to provide consistent care and support so that children can develop confidence and self-worth.
Through our curriculum and daily interactions, children are helped to:
This supports them not only in school, but in all aspects of life.
understand their emotions
build positive relationships
develop resilience
know how and when to seek help
Building strong relationships
Positive relationships are at the heart of wellbeing at Thatcham Park as strong relationships ensure that children feel known, understood and supported. Adults take time to know children as individuals, creating a culture where everyone feels valued and included.
We work closely with parents and carers, recognising that strong partnerships help us to support children more effectively. When needed, we also work with a range of external professionals to ensure families receive the right support.
Early support and ongoing care
We believe that early support makes a difference. When concerns arise, we respond quickly and sensitively, always keeping the best interests of the child at the centre of our decisions.
Our school provides a stable and supportive environment, which can be especially important for children who may be facing difficulties beyond school.
Learning about wellbeing
Wellbeing is woven through our curriculum, including PSHE and everyday learning. Children are taught how to keep themselves safe, manage emotions and build healthy relationships.
They are supported to recognise when something is wrong and to understand who they can talk to, helping them to feel confident in seeking help when needed. As a result, children develop confidence, resilience and a strong sense of belonging.

As Artists pupils will be provided with the opportunity to be creative and explore their individual interests and ideas. As part of a balanced curriculum, they will be taught a range of skills throughout their time at Thatcham Park such as sketching, painting and 3D techniques. The children will explore the work of a range of artists both well known, local and current. They will practice their styles and then make them their own. Providing them with an awareness of the world around them.
Children will evaluate their own work and the work of artists. They will be analytical and discuss their thoughts and feelings towards a range of paintings, sculptures, and designs by both others and themselves.
Art units provide children with opportunities to:
Build on skills and practice techniques.
Analyse their own work and make improvements.

PSHE and British Values
PSHE statement of intent
Through the teaching of PSHE the aim is to provide pupils with the knowledge, understanding, attitudes, values and skills they need in order to reach their potential as individuals and within the community.
Pupils are encouraged to take part in a wide range of activities and experiences across and beyond the curriculum, contributing fully to the life of their school and communities. In doing so they learn to recognise their own worth, work well with others and become increasingly responsible for their own learning. They reflect on their experiences and understand how they are developing personally and socially, tackling many of the spiritual, moral, social and cultural issues that are part of growing up.
They learn to understand and respect our common humanity; diversity and differences so that they can go on to form the effective, fulfilling relationships that are an essential part of life and learning.
PSHE will support the development of the skills, attitudes, values and behaviour, which enable pupils to:
Have a sense of purpose
Value self and others
Form relationships
Make and act on informed decisions
Communicate effectively
Work with others
Respond to challenge
Be active citizens within the local community
Become healthy and fulfilled individuals
A PSHE lesson
Within a PSHE lesson there will be opportunities for:
Part of the way in which we actively promote British Values is through our PSHE curriculum and the use of Picture News resources across the school.
whole class and small group discussions
stories to support learning
photos and pictures to prompt discussions
drama – role play and freeze frames
big questions
British Values
At Thatcham Park C of E Primary School we are proud of our inclusive school community which is built on our Christian values. It’s important to us that we promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. We do this by providing an inclusive learning environment where pupils enjoy learning, feel safe and make positive contributions to school, their families and community.

pageCache.text:
Music Opportunities
Making Waves: Junior Music Festival
Our choir loved taking part in the Junior Music Festival, hosted by the Berkshire Young Musicians Trust at The Hexagon in Reading.
Following two area rehearsals, which were proudly hosted here at Thatcham Park, the children were well prepared for their final rehearsal ahead of the big performance. They joined several other schools from across the county, creating a truly special shared musical experience.
The theme of this year’s performance was Making Waves, exploring the beauty of the ocean and encouraging reflection on how humans care for the creatures that live there. The children sang with great enthusiasm and understanding of this important message.
It was an amazing experience to perform alongside hundreds of other children, accompanied by a live band and led by a talented conductor. The atmosphere was electric, and the children rose brilliantly to the occasion.
We also enjoyed the journey as much as the performance itself, with a fun bus trip and a celebratory meal at Bella Italia adding to a memorable day.
A huge well done to all of our choir members—it was a fantastic experience and one we will remember for a long time.

Parents
Working in partnership
Welcome to the Parents section of our website. At Thatcham Park, we believe that strong relationships between home and school are vital in helping every child to flourish.
Rooted in our vision, “Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11), we work closely with families to create a supportive and caring community where children feel safe, valued and ready to learn. These partnerships are essential in ensuring that every child is supported both at home and at school.
Supporting your child
We understand that parents and carers play a key role in their child’s education. This area of the website provides the key information you need about school life, including routines, expectations, support and practical guidance.
Whether you are looking for information about attendance, safeguarding, wellbeing or communication, we aim to ensure everything is clear, accessible and helpful.
Growing together
We are committed to working alongside families, offering support, encouragement and guidance where needed. By working together, we can ensure that every child is supported to succeed and develop confidence, resilience and a love of learning.
At Thatcham Park, we value our partnerships with parents and carers and see them as an essential part of our school community: together we create a strong and supportive community where every child can flourish.

Attendance
At Thatcham Park, good attendance is an essential part of living out our vision: “Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11).
We want every child to feel confident, supported and ready to learn each day. Regular attendance helps children to build strong relationships, make good progress and fully take part in school life.
Why attendance matters
Being in school every day gives children the best opportunity to succeed. It supports their learning, wellbeing and sense of belonging. Good attendance is also closely linked to positive long-term outcomes and future opportunities.
Working together
Attendance is a shared responsibility between school and home.
We ask parents and carers to ensure that children:
Parents are expected to contact the school on the first day of absence, providing a reason, and to keep the school updated if absence continues.
attend school every day
arrive on time and ready to learn
Arriving on time
A calm and positive start to the day is important for children’s learning and wellbeing.
Children should arrive at school on time so they do not miss important learning or opportunities to connect with others. Late arrival can be unsettling and may affect both progress and confidence.
Absence from school
If a child is unwell or unable to attend school, parents must inform us on the first day of absence. The school will always follow up any unexplained absence to ensure children are safe.
Supporting good attendance
We monitor attendance carefully and will contact families if attendance begins to fall. Where needed, we will work with parents to understand any barriers and put support in place.
Safeguarding and wellbeing
Regular attendance is closely linked to safeguarding and wellbeing. We recognise that poor attendance may sometimes be a sign that a child needs additional support.

E-Safety
Keeping safe online
At Thatcham Park, we help children learn how to use technology safely and responsibly. This is part of living out our vision: “Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11).
We want children to feel confident when using the internet and know how to keep themselves and others safe.
Learning to stay safe
Children are taught how to use the internet as part of their learning, always with guidance and supervision.
Children are encouraged to think carefully about what they see, say and share online.
personal information should always be kept private
Knowing what to do
We teach children simple ways to stay safe online, including:
Children know that they will always be listened to and supported.
never arranging to meet anyone online
Using technology responsibly
Children use school devices to support their learning in a safe and structured way. Internet access is carefully managed, and adults supervise children at all times.
Mobile phones and smart devices are not used during the school day. Where needed, phones are switched off and stored safely.
Children also learn that taking photos or recording others without permission is not allowed and may be unsafe.
Working together
We work closely with parents and carers to ensure children develop safe habits when using technology at home and at school. Together, we help children to use technology in a positive way.

Early Years at Thatcham Park
A strong start for every child
At Thatcham Park, we recognise the importance of giving children the very best start in life. Rooted in our vision, “Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11), our Early Years provision is designed to nurture, support and develop every child from the very beginning.
We understand that children join us with a wide range of experiences and starting points. By offering a strong and nurturing early start, we ensure that every child is encouraged to grow in confidence, develop key skills and feel ready to learn. Early support and strong relationships ensure that children feel secure from the very beginning.
Building strong foundations
Our early years environment is built on secure relationships, consistent routines and a deep understanding of children’s needs. This enables children to feel safe, valued and able to explore the world around them with curiosity and confidence.
We place a strong emphasis on:
This helps children to become resilient learners, ready for the next stage of their education.
communication and language
personal, social and emotional development
early learning through play, talk and exploration
Supporting every family
We know that supporting children early also means supporting families. Our team works closely with parents and carers, building trusting relationships and offering guidance, care and practical support where needed. This partnership enables us to respond quickly to children's needs and support their development effectively.
Because of our strong early provision, children make clear progress in their readiness for school, enabling them to flourish both socially and academically as they move through the school.
Growing together
Early Years at Thatcham Park is more than preparation for school—it is the start of a journey. Through encouragement, care and strong relationships, we ensure that every child has the opportunity to thrive from the very beginning. Thessalonians 5:11
Aims
We aim to encourage and support young children to:
As a result, children develop confidence, independence and a positive attitude to learning.
Become confident, independent and aspirational
Question, challenge and solve problems creatively
Practice
Our practice is guided by the four principles of the EYFS Framework:
Young children learn through seeing, hearing and doing. They are researchers who explore, test their ideas, solve problems and try to make sense of their world. The intent of our Early Years Foundation Stage – across all 3 settings, Stepping Stones (our setting for 2 year olds), Foundation 1 (nursery for 3 to 4 year olds) and Foundation 2 (Reception) is to ensure that every child is supported and encouraged to enjoy learning, be confident to take risks, ask questions and understand that misunderstandings and uncertainties are part of real learning.
Our EYFS practitioners understand the need to meet the individual needs of all children and plan learning experiences which are challenging but achievable, and which build on children’s interests, strengths and questions. They also understand that young children need time and space to learn effectively and, therefore, each child is given opportunities to repeat, revisit and reflect on previous experiences. Play underpins the delivery of the EYFS and the children have opportunities to explore and extend development and learning through their own interests both inside and outside.

Infection control and Medical conditions
Supporting Medical Conditions
At Thatcham Park, we are committed to ensuring that every child is supported to thrive. Guided by our vision, “Encourage one another and build each other up” (1 Thessalonians 5:11), we ensure that pupils with medical conditions are fully included, valued and able to take part in all aspects of school life.
Supporting every child to flourish
We recognise that children with medical needs may require additional support to access learning and school experiences. Our aim is to ensure that all pupils can participate safely and confidently in lessons, trips and activities alongside their peers.
We work closely with families, healthcare professionals and staff to ensure that support is carefully planned and regularly reviewed.
Individualised care and support
Where needed, we create Individual Healthcare Plans (IHPs) in partnership with parents and relevant professionals. These plans clearly outline the support a child needs, when it is required and who will provide it, ensuring a consistent and safe approach.
Children are involved in decisions about their care wherever appropriate, helping them to develop independence and confidence over time.
Safe and trained support
Staff receive appropriate training so they can support pupils safely and effectively. There is always someone available to respond to a child’s medical needs, including in emergency situations.
Medication is carefully managed, with clear procedures in place to ensure that it is administered safely and with parental consent where required.
Dignity, care and respect
We understand that some medical needs may involve personal care. In these situations, we act with the utmost sensitivity, ensuring that every child is treated with dignity, respect and privacy at all times.
Our approach promotes independence wherever possible, while ensuring children feel safe, supported and listened to.
Working in partnership
Strong communication with families is key. Parents and carers provide important information about their child’s needs and work alongside the school to ensure the right support is in place.
We aim to build trusting relationships so that concerns can be shared openly and support can be adapted quickly when needed.

pageCache.text:
School Meals
"Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing." 1 Thessalonians 5:11
School Meals
The children have a choice to have a school meal or to bring a healthy packed lunch to school.
School meals are provided by Caterlink. Caterlink want you to know everything there is to know about their menus and provide an online ordering system, so that you can choose at home with your child or on the way to school via your phone. You will have access to all their recipes, ingredients listings, nutritional breakdown, allergen and dietary information and even a diabetic feature showing the carb count of each dish at a glance. All meals are freshly prepared on site. For more information about Caterlink please refer to their website.
In order for your child to have a school meal, whether free school meal, paid school meal or Universal Infant Free School Meal, you will need to set up a Parent Pay account. If you have provided the school with a current email address, you should automatically receive an email with all your necessary login details. If you have not received the email, or do not have a Parent Pay account, please contact the school office.
ParentPay - Meal Booking Guide
You can order up to 8am on any given day, or as far in advance as a whole term. Orders can be placed on a pc, laptop, tablet or smartphone. We encourage all parents to order with their children and not for their children. Children are also able to order in the morning via the classroom computer. Please note that any orders made at home are final and cannot be changed in the classroom.
If you need to cancel a dinner on the day, you will need to contact the school office. Otherwise you will be charged, even if the meal isn't taken.
For children in KS2 (Years 3-6), each meal costs £2.60 and must be paid for in advance or on the day.
For your convenience, Caterlink offer several payment methods. Select the payment date that suits you and Caterlink will keep you informed with monthly statements to show which meals were chosen, the amount due and remind you when the money will be collected – simple!
Some children in all year groups may be entitled to Free School Meals via the Pupil Premium Grant. Parents/Carers should contact the School Office for guidance on how to check eligibility.
Children in Reception and KS1 are entitled to Universal Infant Free School Meals.
